analysis.title: Taiwan Weakness
key_insights: The TWSE fell 8% week-to-Thursday and kept falling Friday, trading below 40k for the first time since April. It is also on track to close below the late-July consolidation level for the first time.
Foreign institutional investors (FINI) sold USD$3.1bn on Thursday, a 6th straight session of selling that totals USD$19.2bn. They have sold on 19 of 20 sessions since 10/6, for USD$48bn in outflows.

Local funds have net bought for 18 consecutive sessions, USD$11bn over that period. Year to date, FINI have net sold USD$86.7bn of TWSE stocks (including USD$68.9bn of TSMC), while local funds bought USD$33.5bn (including USD$10.6bn of TSMC).
The retail margin loan balance fell 3.4% on Thursday to its lowest since 8/31. As a percent of market cap it remains near the recent highs and the June/July peaks.

Local headlines point to rising hopes that the National Stabilization Fund will activate. That would be preceded by a formal meeting and press release, so it is believed not to have driven Friday's move. The FSC (regulator) is reported to be meeting later Friday on possible stabilization measures, and the Fund could hold an ad hoc meeting as soon as Friday.
October sales are being released. Hon Hai (2317.TW) posted a strong figure, over 45% of the Q4 consensus estimate in a single month, and opened down 9.4% while much of the market opened limit down.
earnings_insights: Hon Hai (2317.TW) October sales were over 45% of the Q4 consensus estimate in a single month. The stock still opened down 9.4% on 11/6 while much of the market opened limit down.
risk_factors: Continued foreign outflows from the TWSE, including heavy TSMC selling.
Retail margin balance remains high relative to market cap, which leaves room for forced selling.
The market opened limit down on 11/6, and the TWSE is below the late-July consolidation level.
vol_and_positioning: Retail margin loan balance in the TWSE fell 3.4% on Thursday to its lowest since 8/31, but as a percent of market cap it remains near the recent highs and the June/July peaks.

Foreign investors have sold in 19 of 20 sessions since 10/6 (USD$48bn), while local funds have bought for 18 consecutive sessions (USD$11bn), widening the YTD divergence between foreign and local flows.
